bib.title: Fast Inference of Mixture-of-Experts Language Models with Offloading

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Fast Inference of Mixture-of-Experts Language Models with Offloading", Artyom Eliseev and Denis Mazur, preprint arXiv:2312.17238v1 [cs.LG], 28 Dec 2023. No venue printed. Code: github.com/dvmazur/mixtral-offloading.

COVERAGE: all 48,535 chars read (12 pages). Body is pp.1-8, the rest is references. There are no appendices. The paper has no limitations section. The Figure 1 and Figure 2 plots were not read; only their captions were. I did not read the plotted values, so there are no hit-rate or recall numbers.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: The full algorithm (LRU cache plus speculative expert loading) with mixed quantization runs Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct at about 2-3 tok/s on consumer GPUs.
  number: Table 2 full algorithm, tok/s. 2-bit experts: A100 3.061, RTX 3080 Mobile 2.655, RTX 3060 2.278, T4 (Colab) 2.092. 3-bit experts: A100 2.845, 3080 Mobile 2.475, 3060 2.038, T4 (Azure cloud) 1.603.
  setup: batch size 1, sampling on OpenAssistant conversations, pure sampling with no temperature or nucleus. Attention at 4-bit HQQ, experts at 2 or 3 bit. k=2 on the RTX 3060 and k=4 on the other GPUs. The A100-80GB-SXM was run with offloading only as a reference.
  quote: "Full algorithm 3.061 2.655 2.278 2.092 2.845 2.475 2.038 1.603"
  where: p.7, Table 2
- claim: The intro says 2-3 tok/s and Sec 4.3 says 2-4 tok/s. The 3-bit T4 result is 1.6 tok/s, which is below both.
  number: 2-3 tok/s (intro); 2-4 tok/s (Sec 4.3)
  setup: as above. Hardware: free-tier Colab T4 (16GB, PCIe Gen.3), RTX 3080 Mobile (16GB, PCIe Gen.4), RTX 3060 desktop (12GB, PCIe Gen.3).
  quote: "run this model interactively at 2-3 tokens per second depending on the hardware" and "all evaluated setups can generate 2-4 tokens per second with the full algorithm"
  where: p.2 (intro) and p.7 (Sec 4.3)
- claim: The ablation shows each piece adds speed, and naive offloading is far slower. On the T4 with 2-bit experts, naive offloading gives 0.661 tok/s and the full algorithm gives 2.092, about 3.2x. On the 3060 with 2-bit experts it is 0.919 against 2.278, about 2.5x.
  number: Table 2 rows, 2-bit columns A100 / 3080M / 3060 / T4. Without pre-loading: 2.918 / 2.227 / 2.051 / 1.567. Without LRU cache and pre-loading: 2.265 / 1.758 / 1.547 / 1.168. Naive offloading (accelerate): 1.392 / 1.059 / 0.919 / 0.661. 3-bit: without pre-loading 2.683 / 2.024 / 1.857 / 1.365; without LRU and pre-loading 2.055 / 1.595 / 1.346 / 1.061; naive 1.246 / 0.914 / 1.791 / 0.580.
  setup: as above. The 3-bit 3060 naive value of 1.791 looks anomalous: it is higher than the 3060 value without LRU and pre-loading (1.346), which would make naive offloading faster than the proposed variants. It may be a typo in the paper.
  quote: "Naive offloading (accelerate) 1.392 1.059 0.919 0.661 1.246 0.914 1.791 0.580"
  where: p.7, Table 2
- claim: Pre-loading helps most on the RTX 3060, which the authors guess is due to its smaller cache. The 3060 gains 2.278 vs 2.051 tok/s (2-bit) and 2.038 vs 1.857 (3-bit); the T4 gains 2.092 vs 1.567 (2-bit).
  number: none beyond Table 2
  setup: k=2 on the 3060
  quote: "Using pre-loading appears to be most beneficial on RTX 3060, possibly due to lower LRU cache size."
  where: p.7. Note the T4 gain is larger than the 3060 gain in absolute terms, so the claim is questionable.
- claim: The desktop RTX 3060 performs about the same as the higher-end 3080 Mobile. The authors attribute this to a host-to-device PCIe bottleneck.
  number: none
  quote: "RTX 3060 (desktop) performs nearly equally with a much higher end 3080 Mobile. We attribute this to the fact that both GPUs are still bottlenecked by host-to-device bandwidth"
  where: p.7. Table 2 shows 2.278 vs 2.655 tok/s (2-bit), so "nearly equal" is loose.
- claim: Quantization trade-off. Experts are 96.6% of the parameters, so they should be quantized harder than attention.
  number: 46.7B total parameters, 45.1B in experts (96.6%). Table 1, Mixtral-8x7B base: FP16 is 86.99 GB, Wiki2 3.59, C4 6.52, MMLU 70.51%. Attention 4-bit with experts 2-bit is 17.54 GB, Wiki2 4.61, C4 7.42, MMLU 65.58%. Attention 4-bit with experts 3-bit is 21.37 GB, Wiki2 4.05, C4 6.87, MMLU 68.47%. Attention 2-bit with experts 2-bit is 17.30 GB, MMLU 55.26%. Reference: Mistral-7B 4-bit has Wiki2 5.03, C4 7.56, MMLU 61.3%.
  setup: HQQ data-free quantization. 4-bit uses group size 64 and scale group 256; 3-bit uses 64 and 128; 2-bit uses 16 and 128. Embeddings, logits, MoE gates and norms stay 16-bit. The 2-bit scheme averages about 2.6 bits per parameter. MMLU is 5-shot. The system evaluation uses attention 4-bit with experts 2 or 3 bit.
  quote: "out of 46.7B total parameters in the Mixtral-8x7B model, the experts constitute 45.1B (96.6%)" and "it seems advantageous to quantize experts to 3 or 2 bits while keeping attention layers to a higher bitwidth (16 or 4 bits)"
  where: p.6, Sec 4.2 and Table 1
- claim: The two MoE regularities the method uses are expert reuse between adjacent tokens and early hidden states predicting later experts.
  number: experts active in runs of 2-4 tokens
  quote: "some experts are active in short sequences of 2-4 tokens, while others are often used with “gaps”"
  where: p.4, Sec 3.1
- claim: Speculative loading applies the next layer's gating function to the current layer's hidden states. It fetches 1-2 likely experts. It does not change model outputs, because wrong guesses are loaded late. The reason it works is that layers are residual.
  number: 1-2 experts prefetched
  quote: "this type of speculative loading does not change the final model predictions, but may reduce latency if the guess is accurate enough."
  where: p.4-5, Sec 3.2 and 3.3
- claim: MoE offloading cannot pipeline the way dense offloading does. The router uses the previous layer's final output, so experts cannot be prefetched in parallel with that layer. Prompt encoding is fine because each layer loads once per prompt. Generation loads per token, so speed is limited by system-memory fetch.
  number: none
  quote: "inference speed is limited by how fast one can fetch parameters from system memory"
  where: p.3-4
- claim: Implementation details: an LRU cache of k experts per layer (k=2 for 12GB GPUs, k=4 for 16GB), contiguous expert buffers moved as a single copy, pinned host memory, and b=4 shared on-device buffers.
  number: k=2, k=4, b=4
  quote: "we use k=2 for 12GB GPUs and k=4 for 16GB ones"
  where: p.5
- claim: Sub-1-bit QMoE quantization was tried and rejected on Mixtral. The authors say HQQ was chosen for convenience and expect GPTQ or AWQ to give similar conclusions (untested).
  quote: "sub-1-bit compression caused too significant a loss in perplexity for Mixtral-8x7B models"
  where: p.5

LIMITS
- No code is released with the paper beyond the repo URL, and no latency breakdown is given.
- Only one model family (Mixtral-8x7B) is tested, at batch size 1. Throughput at larger batches is not shown.
- The cache is plain LRU with the same k per layer. The authors note it ignores frequency and cross-layer patterns.
- The 3-bit T4 result comes from an Azure cloud T4 because free Colab RAM could not hold that model.
- Colab RAM cannot fit Mixtral-8x7B at a reasonable compression rate, so experts must be split between host and GPU.
- Quantization quality loss is real: MMLU drops from 70.51% to 65.58% (2-bit experts) or 68.47% (3-bit experts) with 4-bit attention. This is base-model MMLU, not Instruct.
- No end-to-end quality evaluation of the Instruct model under offloading. Speculative loading does not alter outputs, so it adds no quality loss itself.
- No hit-rate or recall numbers are given in the text. They exist only in Figure 2.
- Future work stated: "further offloading strategies, based on speculative expert prediction".
- Dated: this is Dec 2023, so Mixtral only and PCIe Gen3/4 era hardware.

BUILDS ON
- Offloading: Pudipeddi et al. 2020, Ren et al. 2021 (ZeRO-Offload), Sheng et al. 2023 (FlexGen), Aminabadi et al. 2022 (DeepSpeed-Inference).
- MoE: Jacobs et al. 1991, Shazeer et al. 2017, Fedus et al. 2021, Mixtral AI team 2023.
- Quantization: HQQ (Badri & Shaji 2023), Dettmers & Zettlemoyer 2022 (4-bit optimal), QMoE (Frantar & Alistarh 2023b), GPTQ, AWQ.
- Data: OpenAssistant (Köpf et al. 2023).

CODE: none in the paper.

FIGURES
- Fig 1 (p.4): expert-activation heatmap for layers 0 and 15 of Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct, with LRU cache k=2 shown as gray squares. It shows the locality that motivates caching.
- Fig 2 (p.6): left, LRU hit ratio per layer for k=1-4; right, speculative loading recall for prefetching 1, 2 or 3 experts, at 1, 2 and 10 layers ahead. It is the evidence for the cache and prefetch designs. The values were not read.

PROBLEMS: none beyond some typos in the source text (e.g. "we build can run"). No embedded instructions found. The Table 2 3060 3-bit naive value (1.791) is suspect. Table 1 extraction splits the table into two halves, but the rows are clear.
